project.name: portfolio
project.description: Personal developer portfolio for Assaad Elaouzi: a React and Vite single-page site with an animated Three.js brain, JSON-driven multilingual content, and per-language static pre-rendering for SEO.

nodes.name: ScrollReveal.jsx
nodes.summary: Reusable Framer Motion wrapper that fades and slides its children up the first time they enter the viewport; used throughout the page sections.

nodes.name: ScrollReveal
nodes.summary: Wraps children in a motion div that fades up once on entering view, with a configurable delay and class name.

nodes.name: SectionHeading.jsx
nodes.summary: Shared section header rendering a numbered eyebrow label over a large title whose last word is set in accent italic, revealed on scroll.

nodes.name: SectionHeading
nodes.summary: Splits the title to italicize its last word and renders a zero-padded index, label, and heading inside a scroll reveal.

nodes.name: WorkflowSteps.jsx
nodes.summary: Small interactive explainer used in project case studies: clicking a step highlights it, advances a progress track, and announces its description to screen readers.

nodes.name: WorkflowSteps
nodes.summary: Tracks the active step in local state and renders step buttons with active and done states, a progress bar, and a polite live region for the step text.

nodes.name: content.js
nodes.summary: Thin accessor over src/data/site.json that re-exports language-independent content (profile, sections, stack, experience tags, project metadata, last-updated date) and the featured project count.

nodes.name: About.jsx
nodes.summary: About section presenting translated intro paragraphs, a responsive profile photo with location caption, and animated stat cards in a bento layout.

nodes.name: About
nodes.summary: Renders the about section from translations and profile data, including a lazy-loaded responsive photo and staggered stat cards.

nodes.name: Experience.jsx
nodes.summary: Experience section rendering translated career entries as a timeline, pairing each item by index with its language-independent tags from shared content.

nodes.name: Experience
nodes.summary: Maps translated experience items to timeline entries with staggered reveal and tags looked up by item index.

nodes.name: Exploring.jsx
nodes.summary: Section describing what the author is currently exploring, showing a translated paragraph and a tag list inside a reveal-animated card.

nodes.name: Exploring
nodes.summary: Renders the exploring heading, translated paragraph, and tag list in a single animated card.

nodes.name: Faq.jsx
nodes.summary: FAQ section listing translated question and answer cards written to be self-contained for people and AI assistants; the same items feed the FAQPage schema during pre-rendering.

nodes.name: Faq
nodes.summary: Maps translated FAQ items to staggered, reveal-animated question and answer cards.

nodes.name: Projects.jsx
nodes.summary: Projects section that splits translated project entries into detailed featured case-study cards and a compact grid of other projects, merging each with language-independent metadata such as tags, images, links, and an optional workflow explainer.

nodes.name: ProjectLinks
nodes.summary: Renders live, repository, and private-project indicators for a project, returning nothing when no link is available.

nodes.name: Tags
nodes.summary: Renders an accessible labelled list of technology tags.

nodes.name: Projects
nodes.summary: Slices translated projects at the featured count and renders featured case studies and other project cards, each combined with metadata by position.

nodes.name: Controls.jsx
nodes.summary: Shared language switcher and theme toggle used by both the desktop nav bar and the mobile menu.

nodes.name: Controls
nodes.summary: Renders crawlable per-language links whose clicks are intercepted for an in-page language switch, plus a light/dark theme toggle button.

nodes.name: LanguageContext.jsx
nodes.summary: React context managing the active language, derived from the URL, with crossfaded switches, history integration, persistence, and document head updates.
nodes.languageNotes: A timed flag sequence fades text out before swapping it; setTimeout is deliberately used over requestAnimationFrame because rAF is suspended in background tabs and would leave the page invisible.

nodes.name: LanguageProvider
nodes.summary: Provides lang, setLang, the active translations, and the isChanging flag; handles the timed language swap, URL pushState, localStorage persistence, head updates, and popstate navigation. Accepts initialLang for server rendering.

nodes.name: useLanguage
nodes.summary: Hook returning the language context, throwing an error when used outside a LanguageProvider.

nodes.name: ThemeContext.jsx
nodes.summary: Theme state layer that treats the document's data-theme attribute as an external store, staying consistent with the pre-paint inline script and dark-by-default pre-rendered HTML.
nodes.languageNotes: useSyncExternalStore with a separate server snapshot avoids hydration mismatches when the saved theme differs from the pre-rendered default.

nodes.name: toggleTheme
nodes.summary: Flips the data-theme attribute between light and dark, saves the choice to localStorage while tolerating write failures, and notifies store subscribers.

nodes.name: ThemeProvider
nodes.summary: Subscribes to the theme store and exposes the current theme and toggleTheme to descendants through context.

nodes.name: useTheme
nodes.summary: Hook returning the theme context, throwing an error when used outside a ThemeProvider.

nodes.name: entry-server.jsx
nodes.summary: Server-side rendering entry used at build time by the pre-render script to produce the static HTML for each language.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the full provider tree and App to an HTML string for the given language.

nodes.name: translations.js
nodes.summary: Central i18n module that aggregates the per-language JSON copy and exposes the translations map, supported languages, default language, and language URL helper.
nodes.languageNotes: Language JSON files must keep identical shapes and array lengths because site.json is matched to their arrays by index.

nodes.name: languagePath
nodes.summary: Maps a language code to its URL path: the root for the default language and a /code/ prefix otherwise.

nodes.name: main.jsx
nodes.summary: Browser entry point that wraps App in theme, language, and motion providers, then hydrates pre-rendered markup or falls back to a fresh client render in development.

nodes.name: Navbar.jsx
nodes.summary: Floating glass navigation bar with section links and active-state highlighting that collapses into a mobile menu sheet below 960px.

nodes.name: Navbar
nodes.summary: Renders logo, localized section links, controls, and the mobile menu; tracks scroll position and menu state and closes the menu on Escape or link selection.

nodes.name: CopyEmail.jsx
nodes.summary: Defines the contact email row: a mailto link plus a one-click copy button that confirms in place and falls back to the mail app when clipboard access is blocked.

nodes.name: CopyEmail
nodes.summary: Renders the email link and copy button, writing the address to the clipboard, showing a copied state for 1.8 seconds, and clearing its timer on unmount.

nodes.name: Magnetic.jsx
nodes.summary: Provides a wrapper component that adds a magnetic hover effect to call-to-action buttons, limited to precise pointers and disabled under reduced motion.

nodes.name: Magnetic
nodes.summary: Wraps children in a span whose CSS transform follows the pointer by a configurable strength, resetting on pointer leave and removing its listeners on cleanup.

nodes.name: RevealText.jsx
nodes.summary: Provides a CSS-only per-letter text reveal so the hero name animates from pre-rendered HTML without waiting for JavaScript.

nodes.name: RevealText
nodes.summary: Splits text into individually staggered character spans with incremental animation delays, hidden from screen readers because the parent supplies an aria-label.

nodes.name: SceneBoundary.jsx
nodes.summary: Provides the error boundary around the lazy three.js hero scene, so a failed chunk load leaves the CSS orb fallback visible rather than breaking the page.

nodes.name: SceneBoundary
nodes.summary: React class error boundary that records a failed state from getDerivedStateFromError and renders nothing once a child has thrown.
nodes.languageNotes: Error boundaries still require a class component because React has no hook equivalent for getDerivedStateFromError.

nodes.name: Contact.jsx
nodes.summary: Implements the portfolio's closing contact section, combining localized copy with profile data for email, WhatsApp, phone, LinkedIn, and GitHub links.

nodes.name: Contact
nodes.summary: Renders the contact heading, intro text, copyable email, magnetic action buttons, and location and phone line using translations from useLanguage.

nodes.name: Hero.jsx
nodes.summary: Implements the landing hero with an animated name, localized intro, and calls to action, deferring the three.js brain into a lazy chunk so 3D never competes with page content.
nodes.languageNotes: React.lazy with a dynamic import splits three.js into its own chunk, and the scene is mounted only after a post-load delay.

nodes.name: Hero
nodes.summary: Renders the hero layout and schedules the 3D scene after window load, waiting 1.2 seconds on precise pointers and 3 seconds otherwise, with Suspense and SceneBoundary guarding the lazy scene.

nodes.name: App.jsx
nodes.summary: Root React component module that assembles the single-page portfolio from its navbar, sections, technology marquee, and footer, shared by both the client and server render entries.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Lays out the page with a skip link, navbar, main sections, and footer, wiring in the active-section and glow-pointer hooks. It crossfades the whole page during language changes, keeping the filter at none at rest so the fixed nav stays anchored.
nodes.languageNotes: Any CSS filter value other than none makes an element the containing block for position: fixed descendants, which is why the wrapper resets to none when idle.

nodes.name: Marquee.jsx
nodes.summary: Reusable presentational component module providing the endlessly scrolling strip of technologies shown beneath the hero.

nodes.name: Marquee
nodes.summary: Renders a labelled region containing the item list twice so a -50% slide loops seamlessly, hiding the duplicate copy from screen readers.

nodes.name: useActiveSection.js
nodes.summary: Custom React hook module that tracks which page section is currently in view so the navbar can highlight its matching link.

nodes.name: useActiveSection
nodes.summary: Observes the elements with the given ids using an IntersectionObserver limited to a middle band of the viewport, and returns the id of the section most recently crossing it. The observer is disconnected on cleanup.

nodes.name: useGlowPointer.js
nodes.summary: Custom React hook module that drives the cursor-following glow on card borders by publishing pointer coordinates as CSS custom properties.

nodes.name: useGlowPointer
nodes.summary: On fine-pointer devices, listens for pointer movement and sets card-relative --mx and --my variables on every on-screen .glow-card, throttled to one update per animation frame. Listeners and any pending frame are cleaned up on unmount.
nodes.languageNotes: The requestAnimationFrame guard coalesces high-frequency pointer events, and the passive listener avoids blocking scrolling.

nodes.name: HeroScene.jsx
nodes.summary: React component that renders the hero's animated Three.js brain, loading its geometry through a Web Worker and running the WebGL scene with cortical shader waves, neuron pulses and pointer-driven rotation. It pauses off-screen, honours reduced motion, and leaves a CSS orb as the fallback when WebGL is unavailable.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Vite's new Worker(new URL(..., import.meta.url)) pattern, so the worker is bundled without a static import, and patches MeshPhysicalMaterial GLSL through onBeforeCompile.

nodes.name: glowTexture
nodes.summary: Draws a soft white radial gradient on a 64px canvas and returns it as a CanvasTexture for the neuron and pulse point sprites.

nodes.name: loadBrain
nodes.summary: Generates the brain in a module Web Worker and rebuilds BufferGeometry and Vector3 objects from the returned typed arrays. Falls back to calling createBrain on the main thread if the worker cannot be created or errors.

nodes.name: startScene
nodes.summary: Builds the full WebGL scene (renderer, environment map, cortex material, wiring, neurons, signal pulses, lights) and drives its render loop with resize, pointer and visibility handling. Returns a cleanup function that disposes all GPU resources and observers.

nodes.name: HeroScene
nodes.summary: Default-exported React component that renders the decorative mount div and, on mount, loads a brain sized by pointer precision before starting the scene. Cancels a pending start and runs scene cleanup on unmount.

nodes.name: brain.worker.js
nodes.summary: Web Worker that runs createBrain off the main thread on request and posts back the surfaces, neuron positions, edges and adjacency as plain serializable data.
nodes.languageNotes: Passes the attribute array buffers as a postMessage transfer list, moving the large typed arrays to the main thread without copying them.

nodes.name: brainGeometry.js
nodes.summary: Procedurally generates the hero brain's anatomy (folded hemispheres, cerebellum, brain stem) and a neuron network on the fold crests using seeded Perlin noise, so no model file has to be downloaded. Imported by both the worker and the main-thread scene.

nodes.name: seededRandom
nodes.summary: Returns a deterministic pseudo-random generator closure for a given seed, producing values in [0, 1) so the brain and pulses are reproducible.

nodes.name: createNoise
nodes.summary: Builds a seeded classic 3D Perlin noise function from a shuffled permutation table, used to shape the cortical folds and cerebellar folia.

nodes.name: createHemisphere
nodes.summary: Deforms an icosphere into one cerebral hemisphere, adding a flattened medial wall, frontal taper, temporal lobe and noise-driven gyri with vertex colors. Returns the geometry plus the crest points where neurons can sit.

nodes.name: createCerebellum
nodes.summary: Shapes a smaller squashed sphere into the cerebellum with fine parallel folia from a noise-perturbed sine wave, colored by wave height.

nodes.name: createBrainStem
nodes.summary: Creates the brain stem as a tilted, translated tapered cylinder with a uniform vertex color derived from the sulcus color.

nodes.name: createNetwork
nodes.summary: Samples well-spaced neurons from the fold crests and wires each to its nearest neighbours with arched edges, returning the nodes, edges and an adjacency list that signals follow.

nodes.name: pointOnEdge
nodes.summary: Evaluates the quadratic Bezier curve of a network edge at parameter t, writing the point into a reusable target vector to avoid per-frame allocations.

nodes.name: createBrain
nodes.summary: Public entry point that assembles both hemispheres, the cerebellum, the brain stem and the neuron network from fixed seeds at the requested detail and node count.

nodes.name: GEO-ANALYSIS.md
nodes.summary: SEO and GEO audit of the deployed portfolio, combining measured Lighthouse scores with an estimated GEO readiness score of about 79/100. It also lists what is already in place and the remaining actions, most of which are off-site.

nodes.name: PORTFOLIO-REVIEW.md
nodes.summary: Design review of an earlier live build with scored areas, reference portfolios and a tiered action plan, plus code for the three most impactful changes. Its file references predate the later redesign and may not match the current source.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Unmodified Vite React template README covering the official React plugins, the React Compiler and ESLint expansion. It says nothing about the portfolio itself; architect.md is the real project documentation.

nodes.name: architect.md
nodes.summary: Main architecture reference covering the tech stack, directory map, page layout, theme and language state, JSON content model, styling tokens, SEO build output and known gaps. It explains how to edit content and the index-matching rules that language files must follow.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: HTML template for the single-page app, holding fonts, icons, the manifest link and the module script that loads src/main.jsx. An inline script applies a saved light theme and redirects visitors landing on / to their language page, and placeholder comments mark where pre-rendered head and body are injected.
nodes.languageNotes: Fonts load without blocking rendering through a preload link that swaps to a stylesheet on load, with a noscript fallback for visitors without JavaScript.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the private ES module project, declaring React 19, Three.js, Framer Motion and lucide-react with Vite and ESLint tooling. Its build script chains the client build, the SSR build of src/entry-server.jsx and the prerender script.

nodes.name: vercel.json
nodes.summary: Vercel deployment configuration that sets the build command, the dist output directory and trailing slashes. It also applies security headers to all routes and long-lived cache headers to hashed assets and images.

nodes.name: en.json
nodes.summary: English content dictionary holding all UI strings, biography, experience, project case studies, FAQ and page metadata for the portfolio. It is the default-language reference whose keys and array lengths the French and Spanish files mirror.

nodes.name: es.json
nodes.summary: Spanish translation of the portfolio's content dictionary, covering navigation, biography, experience, project case studies, FAQ and es_ES page metadata with the same shape as the other language files.

nodes.name: fr.json
nodes.summary: French translation of the portfolio's content dictionary, covering navigation, biography, experience, project case studies, FAQ and fr_FR page metadata with the same shape as the other language files.

nodes.name: site.json
nodes.summary: Language-independent site data: profile contact details and photos, section order, tech stack, experience tags, project metadata, canonical URL, default language and the structured person details. Its experience and project arrays are matched by position to the translated items in the language files.
nodes.languageNotes: experienceTags and projectMeta are positional arrays, so reordering them without also reordering the language files would attach tags to the wrong entries.

nodes.name: eslint.config.js
nodes.summary: ESLint flat config that lints JS and JSX with the recommended, React Hooks and React Refresh rule sets, ignoring dist, .ssr and claude-seo. It also relaxes no-unused-vars for the `m` motion alias, which core ESLint cannot see used as a JSX tag.

nodes.name: 404.html
nodes.summary: Static, self-styled not-found page marked noindex, with links back to the English, French and Spanish versions of the portfolio.

nodes.name: robots.txt
nodes.summary: Crawler policy allowing all user agents and explicitly allowing AI search and assistant bots such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot. It also points crawlers to the site's sitemap.xml.

nodes.name: site.webmanifest
nodes.summary: Web app manifest declaring the portfolio's name, standalone display mode, navy theme colors and 192px and 512px icons.

nodes.name: prerender.mjs
nodes.summary: Post-build script that renders the SSR bundle into one static HTML page per language with SEO head tags and JSON-LD. It also generates sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt from src/data, then removes the temporary .ssr output.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses top-level await with a dynamic import of a pathToFileURL path, which loads the built SSR bundle at runtime and works on Windows. String.replace is given replacer functions so that `$` sequences in rendered HTML are not treated as replacement patterns.

nodes.name: structuredData
nodes.summary: Builds the schema.org JSON-LD graph for a language, covering WebSite, ProfilePage, Person, the project ItemList and FAQPage. It escapes `<` so the output is safe inside a script tag.

nodes.name: headTags
nodes.summary: Generates a language's head markup: description, robots, canonical, hreflang alternates, Open Graph and Twitter tags, plus the embedded JSON-LD script.

nodes.name: App.css
nodes.summary: Minimal stylesheet imported by the App component that only resets the body margin and sets its display to block.

nodes.name: index.css
nodes.summary: Global stylesheet for the whole site, defining the Deep Ocean design tokens with dark and light themes. It styles every section from nav and hero through projects, FAQ and footer, along with responsive breakpoints, animations and reduced-motion handling.
nodes.languageNotes: Dark is the default on :root and light mode overrides the same custom properties through a data-theme attribute, so components switch themes without theme-specific selectors.

nodes.name: vite.config.js
nodes.summary: Vite build configuration that enables the React plugin and maps the `@` import alias to the src directory.

layers.name: Application Shell
layers.description: HTML template plus the client and build-time server entries that hydrate or render the root App, which composes the single-page portfolio.

layers.name: Page Sections
layers.description: Top-level portfolio regions, from the navbar and hero through projects, FAQ and contact, that combine translated copy with shared content and reusable components.

layers.name: Reusable UI Components
layers.description: Shared building blocks for the sections, including scroll and text reveal animations, section headings, magnetic buttons, language and theme controls, the marquee and case-study workflow steps.

layers.name: 3D Brain Scene
layers.description: Lazy-loaded Three.js hero visual, with procedural brain geometry generated in a Web Worker, a WebGL scene with shader waves, and an error boundary that preserves the CSS orb fallback.

layers.name: State & Hooks
layers.description: React contexts for the URL-derived language and the document-attribute theme, plus custom hooks for active-section tracking and the cursor-following card glow.

layers.name: Content & Translations
layers.description: JSON-driven content model: language-independent site data, English, French and Spanish dictionaries, and the accessor modules that expose them to the React tree.

layers.name: Styling
layers.description: Global Deep Ocean stylesheet with dark and light design tokens, responsive breakpoints and reduced-motion handling, plus the minimal App-level body reset.

layers.name: Build, SEO & Deployment
layers.description: Vite, ESLint and npm tooling, the per-language pre-render script that emits SEO pages and sitemap, Vercel deployment settings, and public crawler, manifest and 404 files.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Architecture reference in architect.md, the SEO/GEO audit, an earlier design review, and the unmodified Vite template README.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with architect.md, the real reference for this portfolio: it covers the tech stack, directory map, page layout, theme and language state, the JSON content model, styling tokens, SEO build output and known gaps. Keep it open as a map, because every later step zooms into one of these areas. The root README.md is still the unmodified Vite template, so it tells you nothing about this project.

tour.title: Booting the Page
tour.description: index.html is the template for the single-page app: it loads src/main.jsx, and its inline script applies a saved light theme and redirects visitors landing on / to their language page. Placeholder comments mark where pre-rendered head and body are injected, which is the first hint that this is more than a plain client-side app. main.jsx then wraps App in the theme, language and motion providers, hydrating pre-rendered markup or falling back to a fresh client render in development.
tour.languageLesson: Hydration (React's hydrateRoot) attaches event handlers and state to HTML that already exists, instead of creating the DOM from scratch as createRoot does. The server-rendered and client-rendered output must match, which is why theme and language have to be settled before React takes over.

tour.title: Composing the App
tour.description: App.jsx assembles the whole page from its navbar, sections, technology marquee and footer. It has the widest reach of any code file in the graph, so it serves as a table of contents for the source. Because both the client and the server entries render it, the same component tree produces the live page and its static HTML.

tour.title: The JSON Content Model
tour.description: Before reading any section, look at the data they all display. site.json holds language-independent facts such as profile details, section order, tech stack, tags, project metadata and the canonical URL, while en.json, fr.json and es.json hold the translated copy in the same shape. The key design rule is that experience and project arrays are matched by position across these files, so editing content means keeping their order and lengths aligned.

tour.title: Content Access Modules
tour.description: Two thin modules expose the JSON from Step 4 to the rest of the code. content.js re-exports the language-independent data and the featured project count, while translations.js aggregates the language files and provides the translations map, supported languages, default language and a language URL helper. Both are among the most depended-upon files in the project, so components read content through them rather than importing JSON directly.

tour.title: Language and Theme State
tour.description: These are the providers that main.jsx set up in Step 2. LanguageContext has the highest fan-in in the codebase: it derives the active language from the URL and handles crossfaded switches, history integration, persistence and document head updates. ThemeContext treats the document's data-theme attribute as an external store, keeping React consistent with the pre-paint script from index.html and the dark-by-default pre-rendered HTML. Controls is the shared language switcher and theme toggle that drives both.
tour.languageLesson: When state already lives outside React, such as a DOM attribute, it can be treated as an external store and read from there instead of being copied into component state. React's useSyncExternalStore hook exists for this pattern and lets a server snapshot differ safely from the client value.

tour.title: Shared UI Building Blocks
tour.description: With content and state in place, these small pieces give the sections their common look and motion. ScrollReveal fades and slides content in on first view, and SectionHeading builds on it for the numbered eyebrow and accent-italic title used across sections. Magnetic adds a hover effect to call-to-action buttons only for precise pointers and outside reduced motion, while useGlowPointer publishes pointer coordinates as CSS custom properties for the card glow.

tour.title: Navigation and Content Sections
tour.description: Here the earlier steps come together: each section combines translated copy from Step 6 with shared data from Step 5. App.jsx imports useActiveSection to track the section in view so Navbar can highlight its link, and Navbar collapses into a mobile menu sheet below 960px. Experience pairs translated entries with their tags by index, the position-matching rule from Step 4, and Projects does the same with its metadata, splitting entries into featured case studies, which can include the interactive WorkflowSteps explainer, and a compact grid.

tour.title: Remaining Page Sections
tour.description: The other sections follow the same recipe, each with a distinct job. About combines translated intro text with a responsive photo and animated stat cards, and Exploring shows current interests in a reveal-animated card. Faq deserves a closer look because its self-contained answers also feed the FAQPage schema during pre-rendering, which Step 13 covers. Contact closes the page with profile-driven links and the CopyEmail row, which falls back to the mail app when clipboard access is blocked.

tour.title: The Hero's Loading Strategy
tour.description: The hero is the first thing visitors see, and it is built so that 3D never competes with page content. Hero defers the Three.js brain into a lazy chunk, while RevealText animates the name with CSS alone so it works from pre-rendered HTML without waiting for JavaScript. SceneBoundary wraps the lazy scene so a failed chunk load leaves the CSS orb fallback visible rather than breaking the page.
tour.languageLesson: React.lazy with a dynamic import() splits a component into its own chunk that loads on demand. If that load fails, the error surfaces during rendering, so an error boundary is what catches it. Error boundaries are still written as class components.

tour.title: The 3D Brain Scene
tour.description: This is the lazy chunk that Step 10 protects, and it is split to keep the main thread responsive. brainGeometry.js procedurally generates the hemispheres, cerebellum, brain stem and neuron network from seeded Perlin noise, so no model file has to be downloaded. brain.worker.js runs that generation off the main thread and posts back plain serializable data. HeroScene then runs the WebGL scene with shader waves and neuron pulses, pausing off-screen and honouring reduced motion.
tour.languageLesson: A Web Worker runs JavaScript on a separate thread and communicates through postMessage, which copies data rather than sharing it. Only serializable values cross that boundary, so a worker returns plain data and the main thread builds its objects, such as Three.js meshes, from it.

tour.title: Styling and Design Tokens
tour.description: All the components so far get their appearance from one place. index.css defines the Deep Ocean design tokens for dark and light themes and styles every section, along with responsive breakpoints, animations and reduced-motion handling. Its token theming pairs with the data-theme attribute from Step 6, and App.css is only a minimal body reset.

tour.title: Per-Language Pre-Rendering
tour.description: This pipeline answers the question raised by the placeholders in Step 2. The build script in package.json chains the client build, an SSR build of entry-server.jsx and the prerender script, with vite.config.js supplying the React plugin and the @ alias. prerender.mjs then renders one static HTML page per language with SEO head tags and JSON-LD, and generates sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt from src/data. This is how the same JSON from Step 4 reaches search engines and AI assistants without them needing to run the app.

tour.title: Crawlers and Public Files
tour.description: The public folder complements the generated pages from Step 13. robots.txt allows all user agents, explicitly welcomes AI bots such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot, and points to the sitemap. The manifest declares the app's name, display mode, colors and icons, and the noindex 404 page links back to each language version. GEO-ANALYSIS.md audits the deployed result with measured Lighthouse scores and an estimated GEO readiness of about 79/100, and lists the remaining actions, most of them off-site.

tour.title: Deployment and Tooling
tour.description: The tour ends with how the site ships and stays clean. vercel.json sets the build command from Step 13, the dist output directory and trailing slashes, and applies security headers to all routes plus long-lived cache headers to hashed assets and images. eslint.config.js lints JS and JSX with the recommended, React Hooks and React Refresh rules, and relaxes no-unused-vars for the `m` motion alias that core ESLint cannot see used as a JSX tag.
